decided: The tag vocabulary gains two entries — dishonest-zero (a renderer or computation presents ungrounded data as a measured zero) and http-response-body-leak (an HTTP response body left unclosed or undrained) with alias response-body-not-drained — per the 2026-08-29 retro, founder-accepted. test-shape and render-formatting stay undeclared-watching at n=1 each.
why: Ingest warned on four undeclared coins; a split key splits recall. dishonest-zero names this library's central failure class (2 shards plus the PR #36 escape are the same class); the response-body class exists under two names in the corpus and merging via alias is the vocabulary's own convention. Declaring n=1 singles would grow vocabulary faster than evidence.
cost_if_wrong: Two vocabulary rows; retiring a dead tag later is one retro proposal. Shards are never rewritten either way.
alternatives: Declare all four coins — rejected: test-shape and render-formatting have one shard each, below any honest bar
Alias http-response-body-leak into a broader resource-leak tag — rejected: no such class exists in the corpus yet; invent nothing
scope: .warden/memory/tags.yaml only (gate surface; this tracked item is explicitly a policy item). No rule files, so rules_version is unchanged and no backtest artifact applies.
